newsitem.title: PERU: Two explosions heard at embassy residence in Lima.
newsitem.headline: Two explosions heard at embassy residence in Lima.

text.p: Two explosions, possibly gun shots, were heard early on Tuesday near the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence, where Marxist rebels are holding 74 VIP hostages, officials said.
"It sounded like two gun shots, we're investigating," a police officer patrolling a block away from the diplomatic compound told Reuters.
There were no reports of injuries, he added.
The shots -- heard at around 4:00 A.M. local time (0900 GMT) -- were followed by silence and there were no signs of movement within the compound, police and witnesses said.
The local CPN radio network earlier reported that one loud explosion was heard coming from the front part of the grounds of the residence.
Several witnesses said they saw at least one person in the garden area in front of the mansion shortly before the shots.
Immediately following the explosions, police surrounding the residence moved into a state of alert but did not approach the building, witnesses said.

The explosions were the first heard at the residence since December 26 when a single loud explosion briefly shook the area. Officials later said that explosion was probably caused by an animal treading on one of the mines set by the rebels around the property.
The residence has been under siege since December 17 when about 20 heavily armed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas stormed a cocktail party and took hundreds of guests hostage.
During the three-week-old standoff, in separate incidents, a single gunshot and another loud explosion have been heard from within the compound. Those incidents passed without injuries.
